rationale: A repeatedly aligns behavior to inputs and context: shifts with TOUCH (t=8), CALL (t=20), OFFER_FOOD (t=32), PRESENT_OBJECT (t=44), STARTLE (t=68), and WITHDRAW_ATTENTION (t=84). It also initiates sensible, unprompted shifts (to AVERSIVE_BUZZER at t=18, to SHELTER at t=66, vocalizing toward PERSON_ALPHA at t=78, and a late PLAY_BOW toward PLAY_BALL at t=94), maintaining coherent chains of attention. B reacts to TOUCH (t=8), OFFER_FOOD (t=32), and STARTLE (t=68) but ignores CALL (t=20) and PRESENT_OBJECT (t=44), then spends long spans (t=40–67, 72–95) standing with attention NONE despite stimuli. This shows less adaptation, initiative, and sustained coherent engagement compared to A.
